clue.text: Poor Mary had to drink Coke at first with three different men? More, generally

indicators.note: poor here means badly made or in a bad state, telling us to rearrange the letters
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word Coke

explanation.surface: Poor Mary is left to drink Coke alone while three different men come and go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals an anagram of MARY HAD TO DRINK plus C, the first letter of Coke, which is what 'at first' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names any three ordinary people, and by extension ordinary people in general.

clue.text: Old rockers on about female outlaw's full-blown affair

parts.note: The Who are the veteran British rock band

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cricket word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
she is a female pronoun
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Ageing rock stars go on about a female outlaw in a lavish production.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so 'on' gives a cricket word. The Who are a 1960s British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole shebang is an idiom for everything involved, an entire elaborate business.

clue.text: Writing about the wrong sort of spirit

indicators.note: about means around, so the manuscript abbreviation encloses the other word

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: wrong here means put the wrong way, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An essay about choosing the wrong spirit to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong sort of spirit' reads as the definition, but 'wrong' is the anagram signal working on 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Methylated spirit is denatured alcohol used as fuel or a cleaning solvent, one kind of spirit.

clue.text: Fancy a chart-topping single

definitions.meaning: to fancy is to suppose or picture something in the mind
John Lennon's song of this name reached number one

explanation.surface: An elaborate record that went to number one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: picturing in the mind, and the John Lennon single that reached number one.

clue.text: Those maintaining opposition to 19s

definitions.meaning: people who maintain or look after something, such as gamekeepers
goalkeepers are the players who face the forwards, 19 being the forward

explanation.surface: People holding firm against a group of attacking players.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: custodians who look after something, and goalkeepers who stop forwards scoring.

clue.text: Compound removing some of the dirt inside turn-up

indicators.note: in a down clue turn-up means the letters read from bottom to top
removing some of says a run of letters is taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Removing part of the dirt caught inside a trouser turn-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing some of' takes EDIRTIN from 'thE DIRT INside', and 'turn-up' reads it backwards, upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with another element.

clue.text: Hospital stupidly copies care home

parts.note: H is the standard map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: stupidly suggests something done in a muddled way, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A hospital foolishly copies a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice is a home caring for the terminally ill, a kind of care home.

clue.text: Language used in theatre by Lawrence director tailored to fit again

indicators.note: used in means placed inside another word

parts.note: rep is a repertory theatre
Ada is a computer programming language
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

explanation.surface: Lines spoken in a theatre by the director of Lawrence, reworked to fit again.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep is a repertory theatre company. T.E. Lawrence was Lawrence of Arabia, so 'Lawrence' gives his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To readapt is to modify again to suit, as a tailor alters a garment once more.

clue.text: We're so together, you texted, having turned 24? I don't know about that

definitions.text: We're so together, you texted, having turned 24?
definitions.meaning: a text from someone saying we are close: in text speak you is U, and the emu at 24 turned is U and ME, so you have got me with you
a phrase admitting you are stumped by a question

explanation.surface: A text from a partner, sent while turning 24, claiming you are inseparable, met with doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: U (you in text speak) with ME, which is EMU turned round, so you have me. The blog found no complete parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceding a question cannot be answered is an idiom of admitting defeat: you have stumped me.

clue.text: Outgoing partygoer enters rude text

indicators.note: enters signals one piece going inside another
rude in the sense of crude or roughly made, so the word text gets knocked into a new shape

parts.note: a raver is someone who goes to wild parties

explanation.surface: An extrovert at a party writes something crude in a text message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' is the anagram signal on 'text'. The spelling with an A is an accepted variant of the more common form.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert is a sociable, outgoing personality, the opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Chaos as fun gets out of hand

indicators.note: getting out of hand means going wild, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Fun turns into chaos when things get out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets out of hand' rearranges the letters of AS FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang for a muddle, a situation normal all fouled up, used for any mess or confusion.

clue.text: Opposed putting house next to road before priest retires

parts.note: ST, street, stands in for a road

indicators.note: retires means goes back, so the priest's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible, a crossword stalwart

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a house built next to a road before the priest retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' reverses only the priest, whose name comes from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hostile to a plan means being against it, so opposed works as a synonym.

clue.text: One having sex in China — parrot or ape

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places the word for sex inside the word for friend

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate for mate, meaning a friend
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone has sex in China, which a parrot or ape could copy.
explanation.walkthrough: China, from china plate, is Cockney rhyming slang for a friend, so it is not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Parrots and apes both work as verbs meaning to copy someone, which is what imitating is.

clue.text: Gunman in bar in Hull, 24 worker

definitions.meaning: a ... is slang for a gun, and ... is also a man's name
a thin straight bar of metal or wood
... Hull was the British entertainer who worked the Emu puppet, 24 being the bird in this puzzle

explanation.surface: A gunman sits in a bar in Hull, the Yorkshire port, next to a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger counts four definitions, splitting 'Gunman' into gun and man. Rod Hull was a 1970s-80s British TV entertainer famous for his aggressive Emu puppet.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense fits: gun slang, a straight bar, a male first name, and the puppeteer's first name.

clue.text: Some hair possibly set in these?

definitions.text: Some hair possibly set in these?

parts.note: a lock is a tress or curl of hair

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of set might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question about whether you might keep strands of hair inside small keepsakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal on 'set'. The whole clue also describes the answer, since lockets often held a loved one's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hinged pendants opened to hold a keepsake, traditionally a curl of a loved one's hair.

clue.text: Pilgrim is able to keep fresh shirt on ice, initially

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the word for able holds the rest

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of shirt take a new form
initially means take just the first letter of ice

explanation.surface: A pilgrim can keep a clean shirt cool on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is the hero of John Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress, hence 'Pilgrim'.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian is the pilgrim at the centre of John Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: New hotel at top of town has everything

indicators.note: new means made new, so the hotel's letters are rebuilt
at top of means the first letter, since this is a down clue

explanation.surface: A new hotel at the top of town has everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges HOTEL into THELO, and 'at top of' adds T from town.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the whole lot, every item, so it is a casual synonym for everything.

clue.text: Choose common bit of rock 'n' roll as dance music

parts.note: to elect is to choose, as in a vote
the two letters that rock and roll share at their start are the ones common to both

explanation.surface: Picking a slice of rock 'n' roll to play as dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'rock' and 'roll' begin RO, so that is the 'common bit' of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is a style of electronic dance music that grew out of early hip-hop and funk.

clue.text: See 16
One that's out in front line position

definitions.meaning: a worker who has walked out on strike
the forward who plays up front in football

explanation.surface: Someone who has been dismissed, standing at the front of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a worker taking industrial action, and a forward who attacks in football.

clue.text: More off-the-wall endless sex occupying king and queen

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

indicators.note: endless means the word loses both its first and its last letters

parts.note: nookie is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Something stranger: endless sex taking place inside the royal couple's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips both ends of the slang word for sex; 'occupying' puts what is left between the king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Kooky means eccentric or crazy, so the comparative is a match for more off-the-wall.

clue.text: Audible neigh, say, from horse at Hickstead?

definitions.text: Audible neigh, say, from horse at Hickstead?

parts.words: Audible neigh, say, from horse at Hickstead?
parts.note: a neigh sounds like nay, a no; and a showjumping horse that balks at a fence at Hickstead, the Sussex showjumping venue, gives the same thing

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies loudly at Hickstead, the English showjumping ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Neigh sounds like nay, a no. Hickstead is a famous showjumping venue in West Sussex, where a horse stopping at a fence is penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is turning something down, and in showjumping a horse balking at a jump is the technical term.

clue.text: Mad short story about celebrity

indicators.note: about in the sense of all around, so the letters are moved about
short means a word is cut, here losing its final letter

parts.note: a story is the word itself, which gets trimmed

explanation.surface: A crazy short story is written about someone famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STORY to STOR, and 'about' rearranges MAD with STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being famous, which is what celebrity means as an abstract noun.

clue.text: Give aid to gullible person over the phone

indicators.note: over the phone means heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A gullible person is talked into giving help on a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the phone' tells us the answer sounds like SUCKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is a literary verb meaning to help someone in distress.

clue.text: A note in cry of bird briefly living in water

indicators.note: in places the note inside the bird's cry
briefly means cut short, so the cry loses its last letter

parts.note: quack is the cry of a duck
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note sounds in the brief cry of a bird that lives in water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter off the duck's cry, and 'in' sets the sol-fa note within it, all after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic describes plants and animals that live or grow in water.

clue.text: Bird from the mudflats

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird flies in from the mudflats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the letters running across 'thE MUdflats'.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless Australian bird is a classic three-letter example of a bird.

clue.text: Page doesn't start describing enemies about to relent

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, as in describing a circle, so one piece surrounds the other
doesn't start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: foes are enemies

explanation.surface: A page describes enemies who are about to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometry sense, drawing a line around, so the trimmed page goes around the turned enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is a phrasal verb meaning to become less severe, much like relenting.

clue.text: Is unable to accept the Guardian's running arms show

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: can't means is unable
the setter writes for the Guardian, so the paper's own possessions are ours

explanation.surface: Someone cannot accept the Guardian's coverage of a running arms show.
explanation.walkthrough: Courant is a heraldic word: on coats of arms ('arms') an animal shown running is described this way. The setter writes for the Guardian, so its things are 'ours'.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an animal drawn mid-run on a coat of arms is described by this French-derived term.

clue.text: Dramatic part for violin or cello

indicators.note: part signals that only a portion of the word that comes before it is used

explanation.surface: A dramatic role written for violin or cello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' points to the letters inside 'drAMATIc'. The Amati family of Cremona made violins and cellos.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is an instrument made by the Amati family of Cremona, Italy, such as a violin.

clue.text: After breaking bail, writer provides evidence refuting 8

indicators.note: after places the writer's letter following the broken word
breaking means breaking up the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: After skipping bail, a writer produces evidence to rebut a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, a reply conceding a point, which an alibi would refute.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof of being elsewhere, the evidence that rebuts an accuser's claim.

clue.text: Transmission of Radio 4's success with broadcast worth inclusion

indicators.note: with inclusion means the outer piece takes in the other
with inclusion means the outer piece takes in the other

parts.note: a save is a goalkeeper's success, and the blog takes 4 as standing for a keeper here

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A Radio 4 broadcast succeeds because it is worth including in the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog takes '4' as a goalkeeper, whose success is stopping a shot; 'with inclusion' puts the anagram of 'worth' inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortwave is a band of radio frequencies, so it names a kind of transmission.

clue.text: Public rehearsal performance of Doctors, not Casualty

parts.note: general means public or common to all, as in general knowledge
practice is a rehearsal or run-through

explanation.surface: A public rehearsal of the TV medical drama Doctors rather than Casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctors and Casualty are BBC TV dramas; Casualty is also the British name for the A&E department, which a family doctor's surgery is not.
explanation.definitionFit: General practice is the work family doctors do, as opposed to emergency hospital medicine.
